sources.mechanic: Limited icon routines guide a robot to light tiles on an isometric stepped map.

transformation: An original robot interpreter on independent continuously moving roofs. Literal routines run without guarded waiting. Flight inherits roof velocity; swept visible deck contacts determine landings. Visible source and destination trajectories determine launch timing. In moving-roofs-v5, one active board also permits external planning of a complete future schedule; sustained fresh feedback is not established.

assets.origin: Original canvas geometry and CSS; no third-party code, art, audio or models copied.

difficulty: Proposed baseline D5; human and downstream model calibration pending.
capture_boundary: Playwright diagnostics are separate from downstream native HTTP proof.

geometry_revision.reason: Independent lateral travel previously allowed solid decks to intersect.
geometry_revision.repair: Each roof retains its independent lift, sway, velocity and ballistic collision rules. All five profiles satisfy 1 - 2*sway - 2*half_width >= 0.02. Static layouts and motion seeds are retained.
geometry_revision.proof: Distinct integer grid cells differ by at least one on a horizontal axis. Convex quintic interpolation remains within +/- sway, so deck volumes remain horizontally disjoint at every task time.

observability_revision.reason: The earlier HERE/AHEAD display omitted horizontal goals, other roofs and the trajectory following a lift boundary.
observability_revision.repair: Every roof displays FROM/TO/THEN xyz and time to the current endpoint; the physical endpoints are quantized to the displayed 0.01-metre lattice and ramp phase to the shared 10-ms tick. All surfaces show the same board, current-roof mark and easing law. No arc or dispatch timing is selected for the player.
observability_revision.prediction_horizon: In moving-roofs-v3/v4, the displayed two-ramp board covers the declared 800-ms delay plus maximum 2000-ms primitive flight; minimum ramp duration is 4700 ms. The moving-roofs-v5 recurrence additionally determines all later ramps from one active board. The two-ramp helper limit is not a physical information limit for v5.
observability_revision.historical_replay: Archived v2 sources, recordings and failures are preserved. Worlds without motion_quantum retain unquantized endpoints.
observability_revision.certification: Native HTTP and capture proof, exact shared paused-endpoint reliability, grouped global expected-optimality certification and human/model calibration remain separate gates.

solid_collision_revision.reason: An additional seeded case exposed misses at a thin corner between two sampled endpoints.
solid_collision_revision.repair: The browser and independent grader now intersect each flight segment with the whole translated deck volume. Descending top contacts retain exact square-footplate containment; side and underside entries fail.
solid_collision_revision.compatibility: Legacy generated worlds without collision_revision keep their original collision replay. V2/V3 recordings, failures and sources remain archived.
solid_collision_revision.solver: Oracle planning checks a dense 20-ms timing neighbourhood and reserves 160 ms for its own pointer gesture. This does not change the downstream harness or action adapter.

grouped_observability_revision.reason: The older bounded board did not describe future correlations of a hidden seeded goal stream.
grouped_observability_revision.repair: Replace future hidden-seed queries with a displayed invertible finite-field lift controller. Its current FROM/TO pair, physical BASE Z, phase and printed coefficients determine every past and future ramp. All seeds enter only the initialization. The exact native clock and inputs remain untouched.
grouped_observability_revision.period: Primitive companion matrices have p^2-1 ramp periods (44,520 through 63,000), over 500 times the shift. No pair can repeat during the finite 600-second episode.
grouped_observability_revision.history: V2-v4 truth worlds retain their old motion flags and exact grader replay. Original environments, audits, failures, films and exports stay intact.
grouped_observability_revision.limits: Native coverage and protocol findings are version/source-bound in separate reports. An external planner can reconstruct a complete schedule from one active board; native robustness of that shortcut needs its own check. This is distinct from a no-further-action pre-run routine. Semantic state reconstruction does not establish universal optimality under native timing uncertainty or screenshot-only model competence.

visible_input_receipt_revision.reason: Own HTTP request timestamps and X-server acknowledgement do not specify the browser acceptance tick, and edited slots do not reveal the already-running routine.
visible_input_receipt_revision.repair: Both surfaces print the latest accepted dispatch tick, source roof, heading and frozen literal command list. Busy, empty and ineffective dispatches do not overwrite it; subsequent routine edits preserve it. Turn, centering and LIGHT durations are visible. Motion, geometry, input effects, grading and all profile margins are unchanged.
visible_input_receipt_revision.information_argument: The current exact trajectory board reconstructs every past roof pose. Each accepted dispatch begins ready and centered. Replaying its at-most-four printed commands from its printed roof, heading and tick reconstructs flight, centering, pending LIGHT and immutable queue; current visible lamps supply earlier lighting. Expired busy timestamps and earlier step records have no future physical effect.
visible_input_receipt_revision.validation_boundary: Numerical and headless rendered checks are implementation evidence. Native execution of this renderer and the declared one-board HTTP shortcut challenges remain pending the existing preserved queue. No screenshot-only optimal policy, construction approval or shared-runtime reliability is claimed.
visible_input_receipt_revision.begin_feedback: BEGIN synchronously draws the active board and READY state while task time remains zero. This removes an active-before-first-paint history with trajectory fields still withheld; no clock or mode branch is added.
